<img src="https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/gamlss2.png" align="right" alt="gamlss2 logo" width="120" />

The `gamlss2` package provides infrastructure for generalized additive models
for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS) and distributional regression more
generally. It reimplements the classic
[`gamlss`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=gamlss) framework with an emphasis
on estimation speed and flexible model components. Its modular design supports
alternative estimation algorithms, Bayesian sampling, and model terms such as
regression trees and forests.

Models can use smooth terms from
[`mgcv`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mgcv), custom special terms, and
response families with more than four parameters. Separate predictors for
the distribution parameters are specified in a single formula.

## Choosing a vignette

Start with [First Steps](firststeps.html) to fit a seasonal model for daily
motorcycle counts, inspect its residuals, and predict the probability of a
busy day.

| If you want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Estimate a mean or quantile, or construct an interval for a future observation | [Prediction and Uncertainty](prediction.html) |
| Compare predictive distributions using calibration plots and scoring rules | [Forecasting and Assessment](topmodels.html) |
| Fit a model by Bayesian sampling and interpret posterior draws | [Bayesian GAMLSS](bayesian.html) |
| Adapt a distribution for truncation, censoring, rounding, or extra point masses | [Family Extensions](family_extensions.html) |
| Implement a response distribution or connect one from `distributions3` | [Family Objects](families.html) |
| Add a predictor term with its own fitting and prediction methods | [Special Model Terms](specials.html) |

## Function reference

[`gamlss2()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/gamlss2.html) fits the model
using the [`RS()` optimizer](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/RS_CG.html) by default.
Use `summary()` and [`plot()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/plots.html)
to inspect a fit and [`predict()`](https://gamlss-dev.github.io/gamlss2/man/predict.gamlss2.html)
to obtain fitted distributions. To browse all manual pages in R, use

```{r}
#| eval: false
help(package = "gamlss2")
```

## Installation

The development version of `gamlss2` can be installed via

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("gamlss2",
  repos = c("https://gamlss-dev.R-universe.dev",
            "https://cloud.R-project.org"))
```
